A Japanese reading companion

About Kō

A little help, wherever you read.

What’s new

一About the project

Kō helps you read Japanese on webpages and in Google Docs. It adds furigana above kanji, offers a roomier reading panel, and remembers your preferred pronunciations while keeping the original text and formatting intact.

Choose Try word forms on supported verbs and adjectives to expand the playground inside word details. Explore い／な adjectives with basic predicates, forms before nouns, adverbial and linking forms, conditions, and become/make constructions. Existing verb forms, illustrated mimetics, and Meaning Forks remain available. The original passage stays visible; Reset restores its exact spelling.

Open Playgrounds from the extension menu or Reading view. Word forms accepts dictionary-form verbs and adjectives; Mimetics searches 90 expressions. Dictionary searches Japanese words/readings and English meanings locally, with distinct senses and Japanese definitions. Missing meanings offer an explicit Look up online action. Grammar’s Sentence Lens covers N5–N1 with original examples, selectable construction highlights, formation notes, 18 comparisons, and optional meaning activities. Underlined example words open Dictionary; Return restores your grammar view. The four tools keep their state within the session. Grammar works entirely offline; no search or learning history is saved.

Built by Gonzalo Cibeira to make reading Japanese in Google Docs easier, then extended to help wherever you browse. Kō is source available under the Kō No-Resale License 1.0. You may use it freely, including at work, modify it, and share it for free. Selling Kō or modified or rebranded copies, or charging for access, requires written permission from Gonzalo Cibeira. Earlier MIT-distributed copies retain their original permissions.

二Reading settings

Open Kō from Chrome’s extensions toolbar to pause automatic readings, choose your reading appearance, enable the reading panel, or manage local pronunciation corrections. Site settings apply to the webpage you have open.

Mimetics use new ukiyo-e-inspired pixel dioramas by default. Turn this on to use the original line animations. This choice applies to all sites and is saved on this device.

Kōくん

An optional animated companion, off by default. Turn him on in the extension popup, then drag him around the webpage or hover over a Japanese word for an offline reading. You can choose highlight mode, size, and a still character. His position is remembered per site. Optional English and Japanese definitions use bundled dictionaries first, with Wiktionary online fallback for missing meanings. His switch works independently of automatic page readings; Pause on this site hides him.

三Privacy

Furigana and grammar exploration run on your device with bundled resources. Dictionary Playground contacts Wiktionary only after its explicit online action. Reading-panel and enabled Kōくん definitions follow the local-first automatic fallback described here. Settings, corrections, animation choices, Kōくん positions per site, and update-announcement dismissals are stored locally; playground searches, typed verbs, and experiments stay in memory without a saved history. Clicking a word in the reading panel looks up English meanings in bundled JMdict and Japanese definitions in a bundled Japanese Wiktionary snapshot. Wiktionary is contacted only when the selected language’s local lookup misses or cannot load. Kōくん definitions start off; when enabled, the selected language follows the same local-first lookup. Online requests send only dictionary-form lookup terms and any spelling-reference terms; Wikimedia also receives your IP address. Surrounding sentences and full documents are not uploaded. Kō has no analytics, advertising, or extension account.

Dictionary source

English meanings use JMdict, copyright James William Breen and the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG), under CC BY-SA 4.0. Kō converts the data into indexed lookup shards; this third-party dictionary remains under its own licence.

JMdict project ↗ · EDRDG terms · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Dictionary documentation

Japanese definitions

Japanese explanations use Japanese Wiktionary contributors’ data extracted by Kaikki/Wiktextract, under CC BY-SA 4.0. Kō filters Japanese entries, resolves unique spelling references, and creates compressed lookup shards. Coverage is incomplete; Reading view and enabled Kōくん definitions fall back online, while Dictionary Playground offers an explicit online action.

五What’s new · Changelog

1.4.0 · Unreleased (WIP)

Read the 1.4.0 release notes

Work in progress: explore Japanese words and N5–N1 grammar in two new playgrounds, with local search and Sentence Lens comparisons. Version 1.4 has not been released.

  • Dictionary: search Japanese spellings, readings, and English meanings in bundled JMdict. Browse separate entries and expandable senses with reading restrictions, parts of speech, usage labels, source attribution, and local Japanese definitions. Show more loads the next 30 results.
  • Explicit online lookup: Dictionary Playground makes no automatic online requests. Missing definitions offer a language-specific action sending only the selected Japanese term to Wiktionary. Reading view and Kōくん retain their existing local-first fallback policy.
  • Grammar — Sentence Lens: 847 original Kō grammar points reconcile 848 N5–N1 reference entries, with three original annotated examples each. Browse levels and meaning groups, search Japanese/kana/romaji/English, inspect highlighted constructions, and expand formation and usage notes.
  • Compare meaning: 18 original comparison families cover particles, conditionals, reasons, aspect, purpose, decisions, expectations and obligations, recent completion, concession, inference, qualified negatives, unexpected inclusion, and time windows. Complete authored sentence variants show all necessary surrounding changes. Optional activities give explanatory feedback without scores or progression.
  • Connected exploration: Dictionary, Word forms, Grammar, and Mimetics share standalone and Reading-view access. Tools retain their state during the session; grammar vocabulary links to Dictionary and returns to the same example and comparison.
  • Grammar content and indexes are bundled. Ordinary builds use pinned local sources without downloading lessons or dictionaries. JLPT Sensei topic indexes guide coverage; original explanations and examples are Kō material. JLPT levels are supplementary study references.
  • No new dependencies, extension permissions, saved searches, or learning history. Existing settings and corrections remain compatible. GitHub release and store publication are managed separately.

See the 1.4 validation audit for exact coverage and validation results.
